accuracy.evidence: Tooth types, jobs and counts checked against the NHS pages on teeth (children's teeth, wisdom teeth) and the Oral Health Foundation: adults have 8 incisors, 4 canines, 8 premolars and 12 molars (32 including the 4 wisdom teeth; 28 before they erupt), each quarter running 2 incisors, 1 canine, 2 premolars, 3 molars from the midline; children have 20 primary (milk) teeth, 2 incisors, 1 canine and 2 molars per quarter and no premolars, which start to fall out at about age 6. Jobs follow the National Curriculum Y4 non-statutory guidance and BBC Bitesize KS2 'Types of teeth': incisors cut and bite, canines grip and tear, premolars crush, molars grind. Animal examples checked: lions and wolves have long canines and slicing carnassial cheek teeth; horses crop with incisors and grind with flat ridged cheek teeth; rabbits have ever-growing incisors and no canines; pigs are omnivores with tusks (canines) and bunodont molars. Parameterised answers (8n, 20 − n, 3n, 2n) were enumerated by the validator.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the mistakes teachers report for this Year 4 objective (Primary Science Teaching Trust and Science Learning Hub notes on teeth): all teeth are the same shape in different sizes (step 1 predict), every back tooth is a molar so premolars are missed (step 3 quarter builder hint and m9), canines are for chewing (step 2 predict, m8, challenge tag tear), confusing the 20 milk teeth with 32 adult teeth (predict in step 3, challenge tags milk and wisdom), and 'no canines means it cannot eat' for herbivores (challenge tag nocanine). Each slip has its own feedback.

lab_distinct.evidence: gate_lab_distinct passed. 611 The digestive system (flaggut) follows food through the gut and 497 Herbivores, carnivores and omnivores (flagdiet) sorts animals by food; neither looks at tooth shape. Only this lab has a tappable jaw arch in a U with four drawn tooth shapes, matching eating jobs to tooth columns, a front-to-back quarter builder that checks each place and multiplies by four, and diet sorting from tooth descriptions.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner finds the four shapes before any are named (tapping colours every tooth of that type and states shape and job), then tests jobs against shapes with four foods, then discovers 32 and 20 by building a quarter and seeing 8 × 4 and 5 × 4, with the wrong-place hints describing shape rather than giving the name. Sorting six animals applies shape-to-job to diet. Banners state each rule only after the task is won.

predictions.evidence: Four locked predictions with tempting wrong options: 'Yes: teeth are all the same' and 'Only the size changes', 'The pointed canines' for grinding a nut, 20 or 50 for the adult total, and 'Grass' or 'Only soft fruit' for the long-canine skull. The task that follows disproves each wrong option on screen, and the task message reports whether the prediction was right.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions with tagged wrong answers: grind, cut and tear (which tooth does which job, with position), milk (20 is the child set), wisdom (28 is the adult set before wisdom teeth), plant, fruit and meat (diet from tooth shape) and nocanine (rabbits and horses eat well without canines). Each tag has its own specific message; correct answers build a streak.

readability.evidence: Kid text scores Flesch-Kincaid 2.4 (limit 6.5) and adult text 7.2 (limit 9.5). The precise Year 4 terms incisor, canine, premolar, molar, milk teeth, herbivore, carnivore and omnivore are each paired with a plain shape and job description, sentences are short, and buttons say exactly what happens ('Add: Canine', 'Lion: Meat eater (carnivore)').

no_filler.evidence: gate_content found no filler phrases and the explanation is under 12% similar to every other lesson. Each kid paragraph adds one idea (types exist, shape and job, counting quarters and milk teeth, animal teeth and diet); the adult text gives standards and sources, the task sequence and specific common mistakes, with nothing repeated from other lessons.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px screenshots in dark and light themes at every step before and after Show me (/workspace/wn2353-shots/teeth-*). The jaw was redrawn as a U so the 16 teeth no longer overlap; food cards were enlarged to 42 px with 12 px text; animal cards were made 76 px tall on phones so names and tooth descriptions do not collide; the quarter builder shows 8 slots and 4 large tooth tiles in one row with nothing clipped.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed on desktop and iPhone 13 with axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes and no console errors. Every canvas action has a button (Tap tooth n, Pick then match a job to a tooth type, Add: tooth type, Pick then choose a diet), the canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action with what is found, placed or left, and feedback is spoken with c.say.
